title: The Upkeep Rebate applies automatically to Prime Agents' cross-holdings, so upkeep is not charged twice on the same value
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.3.2.2.1.1 states the entitlement and then explains its own emptiness: "every Prime Agent is entitled to the Upkeep Rebate Primitive for tokens of other Prime Agents that they hold. Because this right automatically applies, there are no parameters."

The problem it solves follows from how the Upkeep Fee is assessed. If each Prime Agent pays on its own market capitalization, and Agent A's market cap partly reflects the Agent B tokens sitting on A's balance sheet, then the same value is charged twice — once inside B's market cap and again inside A's. The rebate nets that out.

What makes this more than an accounting nicety is the behaviour it protects. Without a rebate, the fee would penalize Agents for holding each other's tokens, discouraging exactly the cross-Agent alignment the ecosystem wants; with it, an Agent can take a position in another Agent without paying upkeep on it twice. A.6.1.1.3.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1 supports the calculation operationally by requiring that "Keel keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account" — one auditable address rather than a portfolio to reconstruct.

Declaring the Primitive parameterless is itself a design statement: the rebate is a structural right of being a Prime Agent, not something each Agent negotiates.
description: Every Prime Agent is entitled to a rebate for other Prime Agents' tokens it holds; the entitlement is parameterless by design and is netted directly against the fee owed.
